overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: at most four of the nine members participated in the Facebook group, below the five-member quorum, so no deliberation occurred.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee deliberated on a wind turbine project through a closed Facebook group with committee members participating.
allegations.key_passage: Because a quorum of the Committee is five members, and at most four members participated in the Facebook Group, no deliberation occurred.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the chair created a closed Facebook group to facilitate private deliberations among committee members on the wind turbine.
allegations.key_passage: We find no evidence that a fifth member of the Committee was ever a member of the Facebook Group or communicated via the Facebook Group.

allegations.summary: Committee argued the Facebook group communications were political speech, not matters within its jurisdiction; the AG did not reach this argument.
allegations.key_passage: we need not address the Committee's argument in its April 6, 2012 letter that the members' communications via the Facebook Group consisted of political speech, and therefore were not matters within the Committee's jurisdiction.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
